educationalGoal: To foster intelligence, sensitivity, and virtue, we will pick up philosophical thoughts and try to acquire the ability to think by ourselves. Discussing real concrete issues with others, students will understand others' thoughts, practice thinking with others, and develop critical thinking skills. Through these, students will cultivate the thinking ability necessary to become an autonomous engineers.
advice: Course Description: In each class, we will pick up one specific issue and conduct group discussions. After that, we introduce the discussions of representative philosophers who considered the problem. In examining specific issues, in addition to the ability to capture knowledge, conduct quizzes with the aim of cultivating the ability to express one's own thoughts, the ability to understand the ideas of others, and the ability to think with others. The topics discussed are, for example, “love”, “beauty”, “lie”, “discrimination”, “animal rights”, “environment”, “government”, and “meaning to live”. Expectations for Students: ・ In this course, emphasis is not on memorizing knowledge, but on thinking about oneself using knowledge. In other words, the emphasis is on critical thinking about specific issues. In dialogues and exercises, be sure to work with that in mind. ・ Let's examine unknown term by oneself using various encyclopedias.
books: We don't have any required materials.
requiredKnowledge: ・ Through newspapers, etc., always take an interest in the real problem and acquire an attitude to consider it as a problem related to oneself. ・ Acquire writing skills through "Basic Style for Study A and B".

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand typical philosophical concepts and explain them concretely.
Be able to express themselves about the process and the results of thinking about specific problems.
Be able to understand and express the ideas of others about specific problems.
Be able to express the process and results of thinking about specific issues with others.
Be able to think critically about specific problems and explain them in clear sentences.
Be able to self-evaluate target abilities for students in this course.

achievementLevels.ideal: 1. You can understand typical philosophical concepts appropriately and explain them in your own words. 2. For concrete problems, you can express your thought process and its results in logical sentences. 3. You can understand other people's ideas about specific problems and express them in logical sentences. 4. With regard to specific problems, you can express the process and the results of thinking with others in logical sentences. 5. You can think critically about specific problems and explain them convincingly with clear sentences. 6. Be aware of the target abilities for students, you can always evaluate whether you understand the class.
achievementLevels.standard: 1. You can understand typical philosophical concepts and explain them concretely. 2. For concrete problems, you can express your thought process and its results in sentences. 3. You can understand other people's ideas about specific problems and express them in sentences. 4. With regard to specific problems, you can express the process and the results of thinking with others in sentences. 5. You can think critically about specific problems and explain them in sentences. 6. Be aware of the target abilities for students, you can sometimes evaluate whether you understand the class.
